fact: Hespress reports that the House of Representatives bureau announced at a public sitting early in the week of 9 January 2025 that it had received a private member's bill on regulating the use of AI, 17 articles, tabled by six Mouvement Populaire deputies, with fines of 50,000 to 500,000 dirhams and prison of 6 months to 5 years for violations (event dated by the article's publication week).
system: Proposed law on regulating the use of artificial intelligence (private member's bill)

fact: A Hespress interview with academic Adel Ben Hamza (published 2026-07-30) says Morocco's legislator wrote into the revised electoral framework for the 2026 legislative elections provisions that criminalise use of AI and digital means to alter the truth or harm the private lives of individuals and candidates, and excluded electoral offences from alternative penalties; it names no law or article, and the date is the publication date.
system: Revised electoral legal framework for the 2026 legislative elections (AI disinformation provisions)

fact: Draft organic law no. 53.25, as laid before the House of Representatives (document dated 2025-10-24, the published date, as it prints none), inserts Article 51 bis setting 2 to 5 years' imprisonment and a 50,000 to 100,000 dirham fine for distributing a synthetic composition of a person's words or likeness without consent, or false content to intrude on a voter's or candidate's private life, by means including artificial-intelligence tools.
system: Draft organic law no. 53.25 amending organic law no. 27.11 on the House of Representatives

fact: Private member's bill no 53 to create a National Artificial Intelligence Agency to govern AI development and use was tabled in the Chamber of Councillors on 17 April 2024 by the UGTM group.
system: Agence nationale de l'intelligence artificielle bill (no 53)

fact: Digital-transition minister Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni said on 23 May 2025 that her department has drawn up, with stakeholders, a draft framework law on AI setting principles, compliance obligations, regulation mechanisms and ethical guarantees.

fact: The Mouvement populaire group tabled in the House of Representatives a private member's bill regulating AI use across sectors, with risk tiers, a national AI committee under the head of government and penalties, in force from publication in the Official Gazette.

fact: Telquel's op-ed says Morocco has no framework law on AI and that a 17-article bill is under discussion in the House of Representatives.
